intro: The Houston Zoo offers one of the deepest year-round military discounts of any Houston attraction: U.S. veterans and active military get 50% off general admission for up to five guests — 2 adults and 3 children — every day of the year. For a military family in the Houston metro, that turns a full-price outing in Hermann Park into a genuinely affordable one.

There are two things to know before you go. First, the Houston Zoo requires a reservation, so book your date in advance rather than showing up cold. Second, the discount is redeemed in person: you show proof of military service when you present your tickets at admission — there is no online-only military code to hunt for.
This is an independent guide — NavyWeek.org is not affiliated with the Houston Zoo. The Zoo controls the program and can change or end it at any time, so confirm current terms when you reserve.
details: The mechanic is simple. Reserve a dated general-admission ticket, then bring a military or veteran ID and show it when you present your ticket(s) at the entrance. One eligible member’s proof of service covers a party of up to five (2 adults and 3 children), so the whole family comes in at the discounted rate on a single verification.

The Houston Zoo uses flex pricing, so the full general-admission price varies by date rather than sitting at one fixed number — which is exactly why the 50%-off rate is worth locking in when you reserve. Because the offer runs year-round rather than only on military holidays, it is one of the few big Houston attractions where a service member can plan a discounted visit any weekend.

One secondary note: Military.com’s Houston Zoo listing reports a 10% discount on Zoo membership levels for active-duty and veterans with a military or veteran ID at a ticketing window. The Zoo’s own admission-discount page does not spell that out, so treat the membership discount as reported-not-confirmed and verify it at the Zoo if a yearly membership is your goal.

The Houston Zoo sits at 6200 Hermann Park Drive, inside Hermann Park next to the Texas Medical Center and the Museum District — a straightforward drive for service members and families stationed around Ellington Field, Coast Guard Sector Houston-Galveston, and NASA’s Johnson Space Center to the southeast.

intro: The Houston Museum of Natural Science gives a military discount on tickets to anyone who shows a valid Military ID in person at the box office. It is a set discounted price per attraction — not free admission and not a family rate — and it applies only to the cardholder. With a Military ID, the Permanent Exhibit Halls are $16 (versus $25 standard), the Cockrell Butterfly Center is $12, the Burke Baker Planetarium and Giant Screen Theatre are $10 each, and special exhibits are $27.

Here is the money-saving catch most pages miss: for the permanent halls, the cheapest option is not the military discount — it is Free Tuesday. HMNS opens permanent-hall general admission free to everyone, first-come, first-served, from 5:00–8:00 pm on Tuesdays. So if you can visit a Tuesday evening, the halls are free; use the military rate only on the paid add-ons you want.
This is an independent guide — NavyWeek.org is not affiliated with HMNS. The museum controls all terms and prices ("subject to change"), so confirm the current rate at the box office when you visit.
details: The mechanic is simple: show a valid Military ID at the box office and the cardholder pays the discounted attraction price. Because it is applied only to the cardholder, it is one discounted ticket per Military ID — not a group or family price. Dependents who hold their own Military/dependent ID, and retirees with a retiree ID, can use it; a veteran needs a qualifying Military ID (such as a retiree card or VA-issued VHIC), so veterans without a military card should confirm accepted documents at the box office before counting on the rate. There is no online military checkout and no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID step.

The genuinely cheapest path for the Permanent Exhibit Halls is not the military discount at all — it is the public Free Tuesday window. HMNS opens permanent-hall general admission free to everyone from 5:00–8:00 pm on Tuesdays, first-come, first-served, which beats the $16 military rate. Because it fills up, arriving near 5:00 pm helps. The military rate still earns its keep on the paid add-ons — the Cockrell Butterfly Center ($12 vs $15), Burke Baker Planetarium ($10 vs $12), Giant Screen Theatre ($10 vs $12) and special exhibits ($27) — which you can buy at the discounted price any day.

One important limit: HMNS is not a Blue Star Museums participant, so there is no summer "active-duty plus up to five family free" benefit here. Active-duty families who want free museum days should look at the Houston museums that do participate — the Museum of Fine Arts Houston, The Health Museum, Children’s Museum Houston, and the Buffalo Soldiers National Museum — while HMNS remains a paid, discounted-ticket visit.

HMNS sits at 5555 Hermann Park Drive, inside Hermann Park next to the Texas Medical Center and the Museum District — a short hop from the Houston Zoo and a straightforward drive for service members and families stationed around Ellington Field, Coast Guard Sector Houston-Galveston, and NASA’s Johnson Space Center to the southeast.
